confirmed: Source identity and version are correct: Yu-Ju Lin, PLOS One 21(9): e0358542, published September 17, 2026; the journal PDF has 25 pages (PDF p. 1 and page footers). The checker read the complete markdown conversion through the references, checked the relevant PDF pages, and read all five separately linked DOCX appendices in memory.

The paper reports one non-randomized within-person crossover. P01-P16 completed human-only first and P17-P32 completed AI-assisted first; sequence allocation was explicitly balanced but not randomized (PDF p. 5, Study design; S5 Appendix, opening paragraph). No randomized people study is reported.

The quasi_people design class and observational context class are correct; core eligibility fails random assignment and the 50-person threshold, while expert scoring of submitted output meets the output-outcome criterion (PDF pp. 5-6, Methods; pp. 8-9, Expert evaluation; creativity-codebook.md sections 3-4 and form-spec.md design_class note).

There were 32 undergraduate design students from Taiwan, mean age 20.8, mostly third-year students; participation was voluntary without compensation or academic credit (PDF pp. 5-6, Participants). These are unique people, not the two conditions added together.

All 32 participants contributed both conditions: 32 participant-matched pairs of concept sheets, 64 concept sheets in total; main paired comparisons use t(31) (PDF p. 6, Procedure; pp. 14-16, Tables 5-7). Counts of 32 analyzed per condition and 32 unique people are supported; n_randomized is appropriately null.

Both conditions used the same temple-inspired cultural-product brief for Gen Z users in Taiwan on separate class dates, with three 20-minute stages and 60 minutes of ideation per condition; concept-sheet assembly had no separate standardized time limit (PDF p. 6, Experimental context and task and Procedure; p. 7, condition descriptions).

The combined AI condition used the public web versions of ChatGPT-4o and Midjourney v6 after a 30-minute training session, with unrestricted prompt iteration. The experiment cannot separate the effects of the two tools (PDF pp. 7-8, AI-assisted ideation condition).

Three independent experts evaluated the submitted materials; scores were averaged within participant and criterion before paired tests. Raters were blind to identity but not fully blind to condition, and used five-level scoring anchors (PDF pp. 8-10, Expert evaluation; p. 12, Statistical analysis).

S1-O1 reported string verified exactly: Creator perspective: Human M (SD) 3.55 (0.491) vs AI M (SD) 4.03 (0.435); t(31) = −5.066; p < .001; Cohen’s dz = 0.90; Holm-adjusted p < .001 (PDF p. 14, Table 5).
S1-O2 reported string verified exactly: Innovation: Human M (SD) 4.66 (0.401) vs AI M (SD) 3.40 (0.552); t(31) = 15.190; p < .001; Cohen’s dz = 2.69; Holm-adjusted p < .001 (PDF p. 14, Table 5).

S1-O3 reported string verified exactly: Proposed solution strategies: Human M (SD) 4.22 (0.411) vs AI M (SD) 3.67 (0.471); t(31) = 8.330; p < .001; Cohen’s dz = 1.47; Holm-adjusted p < .001 (PDF p. 14, Table 5).

The one_line_finding correctly reproduces the recorded means, effect magnitudes, and directions for creator perspective, innovation, and proposed solution strategies. Cohen’s dz is explicitly reported as an absolute magnitude, with direction given by means and t statistics (PDF p. 12, Statistical analysis; p. 14, Table 5).

The main text supports the form’s outcome definitions: creator perspective concerns distinctiveness and originality; innovation concerns breakthrough potential and user or market relevance; proposed solution strategies concern clarity, structure, and feasibility. These are ratings of observable output, not measures of internal motivation or underlying cognitive ability (PDF p. 9, Table 1; p. 11, Rubric development; S1 Appendix).

S1-S5 Appendices and S1 Dataset exist as separate supporting files; their descriptions match source.supplement, and their contents are not embedded in the journal PDF (PDF p. 22, Supporting information; S1-S5 publisher DOCX appendices read in memory). S5 analyzes order differences within the same sample and adds no new randomized study.
There is no synthesis or pooled meta-analytic estimate in this paper, so the synthesis defaults are appropriate (PDF pp. 5-16, Methods and Results; S5 Appendix).
The reported funding is from Taiwan’s Ministry of Education, and no competing interests are declared; no company involvement is reported (PDF p. 2, Funding and Competing interests).
summary: The form correctly identifies a non-randomized crossover with 32 analyzed students, and all three recorded contrasts match PDF Table 5. It omits three ideation-output outcomes, five concept-sheet outcomes, and the dataset URL.
